title: Audience’s New Deputy for Community
body_markdown:
Farah Miller, who has deep knowledge of the evolving online community landscape, will be Audience’s first deputy for Community. Read more from Audience director Anna Dubenko.


Photo Credit: Earl Wilson


After a number of newsroom colleagues came up with a vision for the future of community in 2024, I knew we would need a creative leader with excellent editorial judgement to execute on the ideas the task force came up with. I am thrilled to say we have found that person in Farah Miller, an experienced editor with deep knowledge of the evolving online community landscape. After spending the last several months as the acting leader for this team, she now officially joins Audience as my deputy for community.


In this newly created role, Farah oversees two subteams working to scale our ability to host meaningful conversations about Times coverage: one focused on moderation and community guidelines, and another on editorial initiatives meant to deepen connections between our journalists and audience. She will work closely with me, newsroom leadership and our Product partners to execute an ambitious strategy for community engagement that she has already been instrumental in crafting.


Farah is a systems thinker who has collaborated with Product throughout her career. She joined The Times in 2018 as the director of content strategy for a new standalone parenting product, which was later brought into the Well desk as part of the newsroom. As the Well desk’s editorial director, she helped the desk understand its audience and meet a massive, growing demand for personal health news and guidance.


“Farah has always been relentlessly focused on our readers and how they engage with our journalism,” said Lori Leibovich, Well’s editor. “With that singular focus, she has succeeded not only in understanding our audience, but growing it. This new role is a perfect match for her range of talents.”


After focusing on health, she brought her sharp understanding of audience behavior to the wider Culture and Lifestyle group, where she ran strategy and ops for the six lifestyle desks — Books, Food, Real Estate, Styles, Travel and Well. She became an even closer partner to our team during this time. Farah hired and oversaw the work of audience editors for those desks and developed new workflows and systems which enabled them to incorporate meaningful insights into the daily report and long-term planning.


“Farah’s ability to articulate strategy is matched only by her ability to operationalize it, and her guidance allowed the desks to thrive,” said Sam Sifton, who oversaw her work in Culture and Leisure. “She’s a fierce advocate for our journalists and our readers, and in this new role we should all be excited to see her bring them closer together.”


Prior to The Times, Farah held leadership roles at Facebook, The Huffington Post and


[Oprah.com](http://oprah.com/) . She notes, however, that it was her very first job that set her on a path toward this one; she was a community-content producer at iVillage, a role in which she mined discussions on message boards for stories and sources.


I can’t wait to see what she discovers within our community, and what she will unlock for readers who haven’t yet been a part of it.


– Anna
